items.title: UKPNP Intra Jammu Kashmir Conference Condemns Security Siege, Demands End to Azad Kashmir Blackout
items.subtitle: Historic summit uniting leaders from across divided regions calls for UN intervention, release of forcibly disappeared activists, and unbanning of Joint Awami Action Committee.

items.summary: The United Kashmir People's National Party (UKPNP) convened a historic Intra Jammu Kashmir Conference uniting leaders across divided regions to condemn the security siege and demand an end to the communications blackout.
items.author: The Mirror Jammu Kashmir Special Correspondent

heroImage.alt: UKPNP Intra Jammu Kashmir Conference Summit
heroImage.caption: Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri, UKPNP leadership, cross-border panelists, and global delegates during the historic virtual summit.

body.text: GENEVA / RAWALAKOT, July 13, 2026 — The United Kashmir People's National Party (UKPNP) convened a historic Intra Jammu Kashmir Conference on Sunday, July 12, drawing together political figures, academics, journalists, and human rights advocates from across the historical State of Jammu and Kashmir and the global diaspora.

The high-level virtual summit addressed the escalating humanitarian crisis in Pakistan-administered Azad Kashmir, where millions remain subjected to an ongoing security blockade, telecommunications blackout, and a systemic crackdown on the grassroots People's Rights Movement.

Participants issued a joint declaration forcefully condemning the deployment of excessive force against peaceful demonstrators and calling on Pakistan to fulfill its commitments under international human rights and humanitarian law.
The conference delegates unanimously adopted an urgent charter of demands calling for immediate administrative and legal remedies:

items: Cease State Violence: An immediate end to live-fire tactics, physical intimidation, harassment, extrajudicial killings, and arbitrary arrests across Rawalakot, Kotli, and neighboring districts.

Accounting for the Disappeared and Deceased: Full disclosure of all forcibly disappeared persons, their immediate presentation before independent courts, and the unconditional handover of the bodies of all individuals martyred since June 5, 2026, to their grieving families for proper burial.

Lifting the Blockade and Restoring Communications: The immediate removal of military checkpoints surrounding Rawalakot and affected zones, alongside the full restoration of mobile data, internet, broadband, and public utility services.

Humanitarian Access: Guaranteed, uninterrupted passage for food, medicine, fuel, and relief supplies, coupled with the immediate withdrawal of security forces from hospital premises to allow safe medical treatment for the injured, elderly, and chronically ill.

Reinstatement of Civic Freedoms: Revocation of the executive ban on the Jammu Kashmir Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) and the resumption of direct, peaceful dialogue between authorities and public rights representatives.

body.caption: Key leadership and international delegates addressing the urgent charter of demands.

body.text: The conference brought together influential voices spanning both sides of the Line of Control, Gilgit-Baltistan, and the international diaspora:

items: Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri: Chairman of the United Kashmir People's National Party (UKPNP), who led the summit, detailing the severity of the digital siege and ground repression.

Dr. Farooq Abdullah: President of the Jammu and Kashmir National Conference and former Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir, who conveyed a special message supporting the summit's objectives. Dr. Abdullah was unable to join the session directly due to the sudden illness of his brother, Sheikh Mustafa Kamal, for whom conference attendees collectively extended prayers for a swift recovery.
Mr. Muzaffar Shah: Senior Vice President of the Jammu Kashmir Awami National Conference (JKANC).
Mr. I. D. Khajuria: President of the Jammu Kashmir Forum for Peace and Territorial Integrity of the State.
Mr. Shuja Zaffar: President of the Muslim Front Jammu.
Mrs. Bhagyashree Pande: Journalist, Research Scholar, and Kashmir analyst.
Mr. Ravinder Sharma: Chief Spokesperson for the Indian National Congress in Jammu and Kashmir.

Comrade Baba Jan: President of the Awami Workers Party Gilgit-Baltistan and Central Organizer of the Awami Action Committee Gilgit-Baltistan, who delivered a detailed video address on shared regional grievances.
Dr. Shabir Choudhry: Kashmiri nationalist leader, scholar, and author.
Mr. Ghulam Hussain: Former Labour Councillor and Chairman of the Foreign Affairs Board of the Jammu Kashmir Freedom Movement.
Mr. Mahmood Kashmiri: Chairman of the Jammu Kashmir National Independence Alliance (JKNIA).
Mr. Sherbaz Khan: Representing the Awami Workers Party Gilgit-Baltistan (Germany).
Mr. Jamil Maqsood: President of the Foreign Affairs Committee of the UKPNP.
Mr. Tahir Manhas: Journalist and writer based in Jammu.

body.text: The proceedings were moderated and hosted by Sardar Nasir Aziz Khan, Central Spokesperson for the UKPNP, Consultant on Human Rights, and Main Representative of UN-accredited NGOs in Geneva.

body.caption: Cross-border political representatives and analysts addressing regional human rights concerns.

body.text: The summit saw extensive participation from UKPNP organizers, youth representatives, and diaspora delegates across Europe, the United Kingdom, North America, Pakistan, Gilgit-Baltistan, Jammu, and Kashmir.

Key interventions and policy questions were raised by prominent activists, including Raja Usman Kiani, Asif Abbas, Yasar Arfat Qureshi, Kamran Ayub, Urfan Nawaz, Jamil Latif, Raja Sarfraz, Saber Hussain, Sajid Hussain, Abdul Qayyum Khan, Aqeel Ahmad, Tika Khan Tahir, Obaid Chaudhary, Mudassar Hussain, Sayed Waseem Abbas, Saad Nazam, Majid Bashir, Waheeb Zubair, Raja Muhammad Sheraz Khan, Naveed Khan, Mirza Shafiq Aleem, Sajjad Hussain, and others.

body.caption: Youth organizers and international diaspora participants in open dialogue.

body.text: Reaffirming its core platform, the UKPNP reiterated its commitment to a peaceful, democratic, and internationally recognized resolution of the Jammu and Kashmir issue, rooted in the universal right to self-determination and international law.

The conference concluded with a unanimous binding resolution appealing directly to the United Nations, the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR), the European Union, the Commonwealth, and democratic governments worldwide.
The resolution called on international bodies to take immediate notice of human rights violations in Azad Kashmir, mandate independent fact-finding missions, and hold perpetrators accountable.

Reaffirming its core platform, the UKPNP reiterated its commitment to a peaceful, democratic, and internationally recognized resolution of the Jammu and Kashmir issue, rooted in the universal right to self-determination and international law.
